title: Triskelion / Triskelion coil public-source map
description: Evidence-separated UPI map of the user-provided public Facebook image and the associated Ascension Tools Triskelion product/source material. The map separates historical symbol evidence, device construction, testable electromagnetic physics, and symbolic frequency hypotheses.

user_provided_image.description: The supplied screenshot visibly names the post 'The Mystery Behind the Ancient Triskelion' and shows a circular object containing three spiral coils and mixed mineral/material fragments. The screenshot is evidence for what the post displayed, not independent evidence for the claims made in the post.

creator_source.description: Ascension Tools identifies the item as 'Triskelion Harmonizer – Portable Pocket Orgonite', describes a handcrafted triskelion coil, and lists dimensions of approximately 5 cm x 1.8 cm.

materials_claimed_by_creator.description: The creator states that pocket OG products contain quartz, amethyst, selenite, rose quartz, pyrite, black tourmaline, citrine, green aventurine and carnelian, with variations for larger pieces.

orgone_mechanism.description: The creator describes an orgone mechanism involving resin, metal particles and crystalline structures. This is recorded as the creator's claim, not as established physics.

historical_symbol.description: Triskelion/triskele forms are historically documented in multiple cultures. A Sicilian archaeological example is dated to approximately 650–600 BCE. A modern secondary source also discusses a Norse 'Triskelion/Odin's Horns' motif, but that identification should not be generalized to every three-spiral symbol.

geometry.interpretation: A three-arm rotational pattern naturally supports a three-phase geometric analysis. This is geometry, not evidence of a 3 Hz or 23.502375 Hz physical oscillation.

electromagnetic_resonance.note: The existence of a visible coil does not establish a resonance frequency. A real resonance must be measured or calculated from measured electrical parameters.

reference_7_834125_hz.note: Using 7.834125 Hz as a reference and multiplying by the triskelion symmetry order 3 is a model operation, not a measured resonance.

reference_8_hz.note: 8 Hz is retained as a configurable symbolic reference, not a universal constant.

radio_reference_1420_mhz.note: 1420 MHz is the neutral-hydrogen 21-cm spectral line and can be used as a separate astronomical reference. No causal connection to this object is established by the image.

mirror_loop_test.closure: The ideal threefold geometry closes after three 120-degree rotations. A physical field or signal loop is not demonstrated by geometric closure.
mirror_loop_test.next_measurement: Digitize the coil geometry and measure its electrical impedance across a swept frequency range.

EST: visible threefold geometry in supplied image
creator's stated product construction and dimensions
DER: third-harmonic arithmetic from a selected reference frequency
HYP: the object has a meaningful physical resonance near 7.834125 Hz or 23.502375 Hz
the object couples to a 1420 MHz signal
orgone-energy mechanism produces a measurable physical field
SYM: 7.834125 -> 23.502375 as a symbolic threefold frequency mapping
STOP: Any claim that the image alone proves a physical frequency
Any claim that the object generates or transforms 7.834125 Hz without measurement
Any claim connecting the object to 1420 MHz without an RF measurement

experimental_protocol: Measure each coil's DC resistance and inductance.
Measure mutual coupling between the three coils.
Sweep impedance from below 1 Hz through the highest practically relevant frequency.
Repeat with and without the mineral/resin body.
Blind the analyst to the target frequencies before identifying peaks.
Compare observed peaks against 7.834125 Hz, 8 Hz, 23.502375 Hz, 24 Hz and unrelated control frequencies.
Use an independent instrument and repeat the measurement.
